title: Land Cruiser Prado 120
verdict: America knows this truck as the GX 470. Everywhere else it was the Prado: the same frame and Torsen center diff with a sensible V6 or a frugal diesel in place of the Lexus V8. It's a brilliant tourer as long as you ask, early and loudly, who last looked at the diesel's injector seats.

paragraphs: The 120 is the Prado that America did get, just not under that name. Toyota launched the third-generation Land Cruiser Prado in Japan on 7 October 2002 on a new, stiffer frame, and the next month Lexus started selling the same truck in the US as the [[lexus/gx470|GX 470]], with a V8. Everyone else got fours, V6s and diesels, a Torsen center differential they could lock, and up to 180 liters of fuel in Australian five-doors. It's softer, heavier and cleverer than the [[land-cruiser/prado-90|Prado 90]], and the diesel has a flaw you need to know about before you buy.

story.heading: DESIGNED IN FRANCE, BUILT IN JAPAN
paragraphs: Development started in 1997. The design came from Lance Scott at Toyota's ED² studio in France, whose proposal was picked in late 1999. Toyota built the 120 from September 2002 to August 2009 at its Honsha and Tahara plants, adding Toyota Auto Body from May 2006, and FAW Toyota assembled it in Chengdu, China. Toyota says the new high-rigidity frame improved handling, stability and quietness. The front suspension was revised for reliability, and the 120 shares suspension parts with the [[4runner/4th-gen|4th-gen 4Runner]] and the [[land-cruiser/fj-cruiser|FJ Cruiser]].

The clever bits were in the drivetrain and electronics. A newly developed Torsen limited-slip center differential, lockable for the rough stuff, replaced the J90's center diff. Active traction control could manage climbs and descents, and top grades added Toyota's H∞-TEMS adaptive dampers and electronically controlled rear air suspension. Australians got Hill-start and Downhill Assist Control, and a 4-star ANCAP rating in 2003. A short three-door version (J125) had only an 87-liter tank, with no sub tank.

story.heading: 1GR, 1KD AND THE REST
paragraphs: At launch in Japan, the engines were the 3.4-liter 5VZ-FE V6 and 2.7-liter 3RZ-FE four from the J90, plus a 3.0-liter intercooled turbo-diesel. In July 2004 the new 4.0-liter 1GR-FE V6 replaced the 5VZ-FE there, and in August the 2.7-liter 2TR-FE replaced the 3RZ-FE. Australia had the 1GR-FE from its 2003 launch, at 179 kW and 376 Nm. It's a timing-chain engine, and CarsGuide owners reported 18 L/100 km against Toyota's 13.6 claim. A five-speed automatic arrived for the V6 in late 2005, and 4X4 Australia suggests buying that or the six-speed manual rather than the early four-speed.

Diesels varied by market. Toyota's model list includes KDJ120s from 2002, so Japan had the 1KD-FTV common-rail engine from the start. Australia kept the older 1KZ-TE at 96 kW until late 2006, when the Euro IV version of the 1KD-FTV arrived with 127 kW, 410 Nm, a five-speed automatic and a six-speed manual. In 2006, diesels passed half of Australian Prado sales. Some markets also had the naturally aspirated 5L-E.

story.heading: THE INJECTOR-SEAT PROBLEM
paragraphs: The 1KD-FTV's Achilles heel is the copper seat under each injector. When a seat leaks, blow-by gas gets into the rocker cover, mixes with the oil and cooks into carbon. The carbon blocks the oil pickup in the sump, starves the engine and can wipe out the bottom-end bearings. Symptoms are white smoke and a rattle on a cold start. AustralianCar.Reviews says aluminum seats replaced the copper ones from August 2007, and that the injectors themselves often fail at 120,000–140,000 km, sometimes as early as 75,000 km.

CarsGuide's 2012 used-car review warned that a seized engine could mean 'a total write-off', with a replacement engine costing about A$15,000, and reported that New Zealand owners were having the seals replaced every 45,000 km. Unsealed 4X4 now suggests seals every 40,000 km. The cheap pre-purchase check is a flashlight through the sump drain-plug hole: if the pickup screen is coated in anything but oil, walk away or budget for a sump-off clean.

story.heading: WHERE IT LEFT THE PRADO
paragraphs: Toyota replaced the 120 with the J150 in September 2009. That truck kept the suspension layout and the 2.7 four and 4.0 V6, finally merged the Prado and Hilux Surf into one line, and added crawl control and Multi-Terrain Select. The Prado line finally reached American showrooms as the [[land-cruiser/250-series|250 Series]], badged simply Land Cruiser. In the US, the 120 is still off-limits: the first trucks turn 25 from September 2027. Until then, the closest thing on an American title is its Lexus twin, which is why GX 470 forum threads read like Prado 120 forum threads.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · AMERICA'S PRADO
callout.title: The Lexus GX 470
paragraphs: North America never got the Prado name, but it got the truck: Toyota built the 120 as the [[lexus/gx470|Lexus GX 470]], with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and full-time four-wheel drive. Lexus showed it at the 2002 North American International Auto Show and started sales in November 2002, a month after the Prado's Japanese launch.

That shared hardware is why the same parts and advice serve both. CruiserTeq lists its ball joints, CV axles, hubs and steering-rack boots as fitting the 'GX470/LC120', Coastal Offroad sells one rear bumper for the GX470 and Prado 120, and IH8MUD runs the two in a single GX470/Prado120 forum.

engineering_intro: The 120 rides on a new high-rigidity ladder frame with double-wishbone independent front suspension and a coil-sprung, four-link live rear axle with a lateral rod. Top grades swap the rear coils for electronically controlled air springs. Every 120 has full-time four-wheel drive through a Torsen limited-slip center differential that can be locked, plus brake-based Active TRC. Wheels are 6 on 139.7 mm.

buying_checks.head: 1KD-FTV: injector seats and oil pickup
buying_checks.body: Ask for injector-seat (washer) receipts. Listen for a rattle and look for white smoke on a cold start, then shine a light through the sump drain-plug hole. CarsGuide and Unsealed 4X4 both say carbon on the pickup screen means a suspect engine. Trucks built from August 2007 got aluminum seats.

buying_checks.head: 1KD-FTV: injector age
buying_checks.body: AustralianCar.Reviews says the injectors typically fail at 120,000–140,000 km. Signs are a loud knock when cold, rough idle, poor running under load and worse fuel economy. Both it and 4X4 Australia suggest testing them at every service and replacing them at about 100,000 km, so ask whether they've been done.

buying_checks.head: Timing belt or chain?
buying_checks.body: The 1GR-FE V6 and the 2.7 fours use chains. The 1KD-FTV, 1KZ-TE and 5VZ-FE use belts, and HD Automotive quotes Toyota's 1KD interval as 150,000 km or five years. No receipt means budget for the belt and water pump.

buying_checks.head: Cracked dash and split rear door
buying_checks.body: CarsGuide reports dashboards cracking near the passenger airbag on early 120s, and rear-door skins splitting along the hinge side under the weight of the spare. Check both, and look closely at the door if a heavier spare tire has been fitted.

buying_checks.head: Rear air suspension (Grande and top grades)
buying_checks.body: If it has air springs, check that it levels and holds height overnight. 4X4 Australia warns that self-leveling rear air makes aftermarket suspension 'a much bigger (and more expensive) task' than on coil-sprung trucks.

buying_checks.head: V6 transmission
buying_checks.body: 4X4 Australia suggests skipping the early four-speed automatic V6 in favor of the five-speed auto (late 2005 on) or the rarer six-speed manual.

buying_checks.head: Test the center diff lock
buying_checks.body: Engage the center lock off pavement and make sure the light comes on and goes off. IH8MUD's GX 470 pre-buy advice applies to the Prado's shared system: a seized actuator is an expensive surprise on a truck that's never left the road.

buying_checks.head: Import eligibility
buying_checks.body: A J120 can't be imported into the US until it's 25 years old by date of manufacture. The first ones qualify from September 2027. A '2003 Prado' advertised as US-legal today should set off alarms.

repairs.title: 1KD-FTV injector seats (washers) and oil-pickup check
repairs.time: Workshop-dependent; often done alongside an injector service
repairs.cost: HD Automotive lists a genuine 1KD injector fitting kit at AUD $169; dropping and cleaning the sump adds labor
repairs.symptoms: White smoke and a rattle after a cold start, oily carbon in the rocker cover, and in the worst case low oil pressure from a blocked pickup.
repairs.fix: Unsealed 4X4's advice: if the seats are leaking, have them replaced, and have the mechanic check the oil pickup for contamination. Pull the injectors, clean the bores and fit new seats and O-rings from a genuine fitting kit. Then shine a light through the drain-plug hole at the pickup screen. If there's anything on it but oil, drop the sump and clean the pickup before the engine starves. Unsealed suggests replacing the seals every 40,000 km. Stop the engine at once if the oil-pressure light comes on.
repairs.tools: Injector puller · torque wrench · new seats/washers and O-rings · flashlight · sump gasket maker or gasket · fresh oil and filter

parts.name: 1KD/2KD genuine injector fitting kit, Prado KDJ120/KDJ150
Rocker cover with gasket, 1KD Hilux/Prado KDJ120

repairs.title: Replace worn 1KD-FTV injectors
repairs.time: A diesel-specialist job for most owners
repairs.cost: HD Automotive lists genuine Denso 1KD injectors for the Prado at AUD $2,200, or AUD $2,790 as a kit with lines
repairs.symptoms: A loud knock when cold, poor fuel economy, rough or erratic idle, and rough running under load. AustralianCar.Reviews puts typical failure at 120,000–140,000 km, but has seen them go at 75,000.
repairs.fix: Have a diesel specialist test the injectors first. Unsealed 4X4 says to repair or replace any that fail. Replace them as a set with new seats and O-rings, and new high-pressure lines if you buy the kit, then clear the codes and road-test. AustralianCar.Reviews links worn injectors on the 2006–09 Euro IV engine to cracked pistons, which is why it suggests servicing them every 100,000 km.
repairs.tools: Diesel diagnostic scan/test equipment (specialist) · injector puller · torque wrench

parts.name: Genuine Denso 1KD-FTV injector kit with lines and fitting kit, Hilux N70/Prado

repairs.title: 1KD-FTV timing belt and water pump
repairs.time: ≈ 1.5–2 hours of workshop time with the water pump (HD Automotive)
repairs.cost: HD Automotive's genuine 1KD belt kit lists at AUD $446
repairs.symptoms: None until it fails, and HD Automotive notes the 1KD is an interference engine, so a broken belt means serious internal damage. Interval: 150,000 km or five years per HD Automotive; Roughtrax's UK sheet gives 100,000 miles or 120 months.
repairs.fix: Remove the fan and shroud, drive belt and crank pulley, then the timing covers. Set the timing marks and replace the belt, hydraulic tensioner, idler pulley and front cam and crank seals (all in the genuine kit). Unsealed 4X4 says to replace the water pump with the belt, or before 150,000 km anyway, and to check the drive-belt idler bearings while you're there. Turn the engine over by hand to confirm the marks before you start it.
repairs.tools: Crank-pulley holder and puller · seal puller · torque wrench · factory manual for torques and marks

parts.name: Genuine 1KD timing belt kit (belt, hydraulic tensioner, idler, seals)
Aisin two-piece water pump, 1KD Prado KDJ120/KDJ150

repairs.title: Clean a carboned-up 1KD intake and EGR, then fit a catch can
repairs.cost: HD Automotive's 1KD intake-clean gasket kit lists at AUD $230
repairs.symptoms: Reduced performance and a choked, flat feel on a high-kilometer common-rail diesel.
repairs.fix: Oily exhaust gas fed back through the EGR coats the intake in carbon on any common-rail diesel with EGR, the 1KD included. Remove the intake plumbing and EGR parts, scrape and clean them (or use a chemical clean), and refit with new gaskets. Then fit an oil separator (catch can) so oil mist is trapped before it gets back into the intake. Unsealed points out that blanking the EGR is illegal for road use.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets · scrapers and solvent · new intake gaskets · catch-can kit

repairs.title: Front lower ball joints
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day for both sides
repairs.symptoms: Torn boots weeping grease, clunks over bumps, vague steering.
repairs.fix: It's the same front end as the GX 470. Support the truck, remove the wheel and separate the lower ball joint from the knuckle and arm. Then either press in a new joint (owners cite MOOG and Sankei 555 replacements) or fit a complete lower arm with joint and bushings. Make sure the grease fitting faces somewhere you can reach, grease the new joint if it came dry, and get an alignment. On KDSS-equipped GX 470s, buy KDSS-specific parts.
repairs.tools: Ball-joint press · joint separator · torque wrench · grease gun

parts.name: SuperPro front lower control arm set, LC120/GX470 non-KDSS (SUSTRC481)

repairs.title: Replace a front wheel bearing hub
repairs.cost: A complete hub assembly bolts in, so no press is needed
repairs.symptoms: A growl or vibration from one front corner that changes with speed or load.
repairs.fix: This is the same hub as the GX 470, FJ Cruiser and 4Runner. Pull the dust cap and break the axle nut with a 35 mm socket. Remove the caliper and rotor, then the four 17 mm bolts holding the hub to the knuckle. Once they're cracked loose, switch to an open-end wrench, because the bolts can't come fully out with the hub in place. Knock the hub free, keep or replace the O-ring behind it, and bolt in the new assembly with a new axle nut.
repairs.tools: 35 mm socket · breaker bar · 17 mm open-end wrench · hammer · torque wrench · new axle nut

parts.name: Front wheel hub and bearing assembly, OEM, 120/150/GX470/FJ (FAHUBGXKITOEM)
Front wheel hub dust cap, 120 Series/GX (FAHUB28010)

repairs.title: Rear air springs: repair or convert to coils
repairs.time: ≈ 2 hours for a simple coil swap
repairs.cost: Usually cheaper to convert than to buy new air parts, according to GX 470 owners
repairs.symptoms: The rear sags overnight or sits on the bump stops, the compressor runs constantly, and the height-control light blinks.
repairs.fix: Confirm the leak with soapy water where each bag folds over its perch. To stay on air, replace both springs, plus the compressor if it has worn out chasing leaks. To convert, support the axle, remove the shocks, cut the air lines, pop the upper clip on each bag and fit a coil-conversion kit with springs, retainers and isolators. Most kits are sold for the GX 470's identical rear layout, so confirm Prado fitment with the vendor. Recheck bolt torque after 100 miles.
repairs.tools: Floor jack · jack stands · flat screwdriver · line cutters · torque wrench · coil-conversion kit

parts.name: Metal Tech 4x4 GX470 rear coil conversion kit (stage 1)

repairs.title: Front CV axle or boots
repairs.symptoms: Grease flung around the inside of the wheel, split boots, clicking on tight turns.
repairs.fix: Loosen the axle nut with the wheel on the ground, then lift the truck. Separate the lower ball joint or tie rod so the knuckle can swing, pull the axle out of the hub and pop the inner joint out of the differential. Fit the new axle (or rebooted original), torque the axle nut, then stake or pin it. Expedition Portal's GX 470 project used factory Toyota axles.
repairs.tools: Axle-nut socket · breaker bar · pry bar · joint separator · torque wrench · new axle nut

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The stock size is 265/65R17 on a 7.5Jx17 +30 wheel. ExplorOz owners run 265/70R17 'with no rubbing issues', which matches the GX 470 consensus on the same chassis. 285/70R17 (about 33 in) needs at least a 50 mm (2 in) lift and +50 offset wheels, or some trimming of the body mount behind the mud flap. On 16-inch wheels, a 265/70R16 is a common upsize, but one owner says 16s may need caliper grinding on a 120.

faq.q: Can I import one into the US?
faq.a: Not yet. NHTSA's 25-year exemption runs from the date of manufacture, and 120 production started in September 2002, so the first trucks qualify from September 2027 and the last (August 2009) in 2034. Canada's 15-year rule already covers every J120, but a Canadian-registered Prado still has to be 25 to come south.

faq.q: Is a Prado 120 just a Lexus GX 470?
faq.a: Same platform, different truck. The [[lexus/gx470|GX 470]] got the 4.7 V8, plusher trim and US-market equipment; the Prado got fours, V6s and diesels, and Australian versions got a 93-liter sub tank. Suspension, hubs, ball joints, CV axles and much of the armor are shared, which is why IH8MUD runs them in one forum.

The original injector seats were copper and leak with age. Blow-by then mixes with the oil, forms carbon and can block the sump pickup, starving the engine. Aluminum seats replaced copper from August 2007. Separately, injectors often fail at 120,000–140,000 km. Check the seat history, look for white smoke or a rattle on a cold start, and inspect the pickup through the drain-plug hole.

The 1GR-FE 4.0 V6 (179 kW) is the durable, chain-driven choice. 4X4 Australia says V6s have passed 300,000 km, but it's thirsty: 13.6 L/100 km officially and up to 18 in owners' hands. The 1KD-FTV diesel (127 kW and 410 Nm from 2006) is the tow rig, but only with injector-seat records. The 1KZ-TE has 96 kW and indirect injection, so it's simpler but slower.

Every 120 has a Torsen limited-slip center differential with a lock, plus Active TRC. According to ExplorOz owners, Australian GX and GXL grades had a rear LSD, while VX and Grande had an open rear diff and relied on traction control. A rear diff lock shows up in some markets' specs, but ARB Air Lockers are the usual retrofit.
4X4 Australia calls the 2006–2008 trucks' 2,500 kg (5,512 lb) braked rating 'low'. If you tow, the diesel's torque is the reason to buy one.

faq.q: What fluids and capacities does a KDJ120 take?
faq.a: Per Roughtrax's 1KD 120 sheet: engine oil 7.4 L with filter (5W-30); coolant about 11 L of Toyota pink Super Long Life or blue Long Life; automatic 3.0 L per drain-and-fill (10.6 L dry), T-IV if it has a dipstick and WS if not; manual 2.2 L and transfer case 1.4 L of 75W-90; front diff 1.4 L; rear 3.05 L on a five-door (2.95 L with a diff lock), with LSD oil in an LSD; power steering 1.0 L of Dexron II/III. Confirm against your manual.

faq.q: How big are the fuel tanks?
faq.a: Australian five-doors carry 180 L in total: an 87-liter main tank plus a 93-liter sub tank. Three-doors have only the 87-liter tank, and Roughtrax lists a 95-liter tank for UK five-doors.

faq.q: Should I keep the rear air suspension?
faq.a: It rides well while it's healthy, but the bags and compressor are wear items, and 4X4 Australia warns that air makes aftermarket suspension much harder and more expensive. Most owners who lift convert to coils with kits built for the GX 470's identical rear end.

baseline_service.intro: On a 1KD-FTV, 'baseline' starts with the injectors: get the seats and injectors tested or replaced and the oil pickup inspected before you worry about anything else. Specs below are from Roughtrax's KDJ120 (1KD-FTV) data sheet unless noted. 1GR-FE and 2.7 petrol oil capacities are from Penrite's lookup for Australian Prados. 1GR-FE, 1KZ-TE and petrol-four trucks differ, so confirm in the manual for your engine.
